_description: All lift-related equations used in GARUN propulsion sizing and mission simulation

equations.name: Lift Force
equations.description: Aerodynamic lift generated by the wing in steady level flight.

L.name: Lift force
L.notes: Equal to weight in level flight

rho.name: Air density
rho.notes: From ISA model; 0.905 kg/m³ at 3000 m

CL.name: Lift coefficient
CL.notes: Dimensionless. Set by AoA and airfoil.

constraints.level_flight: L = W (weight) in steady level unaccelerated flight
constraints.CL_max: CL must not exceed CLmax; stall occurs above CLmax

equations.derivation: L = W → CL = 2W / (rho * V^2 * S). Solving for CL gives the required lift coefficient at any speed.

reference.text: Anderson, J.D. — Introduction to Flight, 8th ed., §5.3

validation.method: Compare computed L vs W at cruise condition. Error must be < 0.1%.
validation.cross_check: Level flight verified: L = W = MTOW * g = 982 * 9.81 = 9633 N (at cruise fuel state)

equations.name: Lift Coefficient (inverse — from flight condition)
equations.description: Computes required CL for level flight given weight, speed, and density. Used in drag polar evaluation at each mission phase.

constraints.incompressibility: Valid for M < 0.3. Above M 0.3 apply Prandtl-Glauert correction.

equations.name: Stall Speed
equations.description: Minimum speed for level flight. Sizing constraint for takeoff and landing phases.

rho.name: Air density
rho.notes: Use sea level for most conservative stall speed

constraints.stall_margin: Operating speed V must be >= 1.15 * V_stall per JAR-VLA standard
constraints.altitude_effect: V_stall increases with altitude (lower rho). Evaluate at highest operating altitude for worst case.

reference.text: Raymer, D.P. — Aircraft Design: A Conceptual Approach, §17.5

equations.name: Best Endurance Speed (minimum power speed)
equations.description: Speed at which power required is minimum; maximises endurance for piston/turboprop aircraft and battery-powered phases.
equations.derivation: Derived by setting dP_req/dV = 0. P_req = D*V = (½ρV²S*CD0 + k*W²/(½ρV²S))*V. Differentiating and solving gives V_BE.

reference.text: Anderson, J.D. — Aircraft Performance and Design, §5.7

validation.physical_check: V_BE < V_cruise (44 < 55 m/s) — correct. Loiter phases use V_BE.

equations.name: Best Range Speed
equations.description: Speed at which L/D is maximum; minimises fuel burn per unit distance. Used for cruise phase.

reference.text: Anderson, J.D. — Aircraft Performance and Design, §5.7
